headline: Updates reported 245 Bryant Street approval revoked and inclusionary zoning ordinance tabled; minutes approved.
summary: The finance report listed a trust account balance of $2,077,645.09. Staff also described 213 Main Street, Overlook Ridge, and 105 Salem Street.
decisions: Approved the September 16, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously.
Inclusionary zoning ordinance update was tabled at Rules and Ordinance.
Planning Board's initial vote failed to reach supermajority; 245 Bryant Street approval was revoked.

decision_evidence.quote: Approved on a motion by Angie Liou, second by Brian Slater, and the minutes from the September 16, 2026, meeting were approved unanimously.
OSPCD went to Rules and Ordinance since the last time the Board met, and it was tabled, but we hope to go back next week for it to be voted out to full Council.

the initial Board vote failed to secure the necessary supermajority, then there was a reconsideration motion that met the supermajority threshold, but that reconsideration vote was actually invalid under Section C.1.a of the Rules and Procedures of the Malden Planning Board so the approval was revoked.

New Business:
1. Call to Order
Mayor Christenson called the meeting to order  at 5:01 PM.
Mayor Christenson presented the following remote meeting notice into the  record:
On March 28, 2025, Governor Maura Healey signed legislation extending certain COVID-19 relief 
measures including extending remote meetings for public bodies.  The same provisions which permitted 
multiple-member bodies to meet remotely, or convene in a hybrid manner, have been extended through 
June 30, 2027.  This extension allows public bodies to continue to meet remotely or to meet in a hybrid 
manner, without a quorum of the public body physically present at a meeting location, as long as the public 
body provides "adequate, alternative" means of access to remote meetings. This meeting will be conducted 
via remote participation. This meeting will not include in-person attendance by members of the public, but 
all effort will be made to permit public attendance, in the manner specified below, via remote access by 
internet, and telephone. Public access will also be provided by posting draft minutes, and/or a transcript, 
recording, or record of the meeting on the City of Malden website at cityofmalden.org as soon as 
practicable after the meeting.
Additional information/guidelines for the public can be found here: https://www.mass.gov/service-
details/updated-guidance-on-holding-meetings-pursuant-to-the-act-extending-certain-covid-19-measures
Mollie Ping called the roll at 5:03pm. Mayor Christenson confirmed next meeting is on 
Wednesday, November 18th at 5:00pm. 
 Mayor Christenson, Brian Slater, Councilor Linehan, Steve Finn, Angie Liou, Catherine 
Price were present. Roxanne Reddington-Wilde joined late.

 Others Present: Mollie Ping, Jane Ventrone (OSPCD staff), Dan Grover (Treasurer)
2. Approval of Meeting Minutes from September 16, 2026.
Dan Grover name mis-spelled and fixed before uploading. Approved on a motion by Angie 
Liou, second by Brian Slater, and the minutes from the September 16, 2026, meeting were 
approved unanimously.
3. Finance Report
Dan Grover was in attendance to deliver the Finance Report:
The current Trust account balance is $2,077,645.09 inclusive September interest in the 
amounts of $5,967.77. The regularly reported expenses are September salary-related 
expenses of $200.00 applied, there may be additional expense-related items posted upon 
receipt of details. No operating expenses have currently encumbered. Current interest rate is 
350 basis points or 3.50%. We can anticipate roughly $72k in interest per annum or $6,000 a 
month at 3.50. We are still participating in the Eastern Bank IntraFi Cash Service or Sweep 
agreement with Eastern Bank to mitigate risk and extract yield.
Approved funding recommendations from Oct 2023, Feb 2025, Nov 2025 meetings 
respectively yet to be spent:
Main                    $373,625.11
Overlook           $349,166.52
105 Salem        $400,000.00
Total                   $1,122,791.63
Net funds available: $954,853.46
4. Administrative Updates
a. Inclusionary Zoning-ordinance update and related information
Mollie Ping delivered Inclusionary Zoning updates. Noted that the last significant updates
were 5 years ago and the ordinance sets out a look-back period of 5 years bringing us 
now to this proposal. Mollie noted no big updates at this time. OSPCD went to Rules and 
Ordinance since the last time the Board met, and it was tabled, but we hope to go back 
next week for it to be voted out to full Council. It must be voted on by November 10th. As
a reminder, the updates refer to a few notable proposed changes including: 
o Reducing the portion of units set aside for IZ from 15% to 10% in new 
multifamily projects with 8 or more units. As it currently stands with a 15% 
requirement, developers do not see significant internal rates of returns on their
investments, and we feel hopeful that lowering the requirement to 10% will 
encourage more affordable development. 
o Reducing mandatory parking minimums for projects complying with the 
Inclusionary Zoning ordinance. Currently, there is 1 parking space per 
bedroom that is built. We propose 1 space per unit for inclusionary 
development projects and 0.75 spaces per unit for 100% affordable housing 
projects.
City of Malden, MA
215 Pleasant Street, Malden, MA 02148 ½ Phone: 781-397-7000 Ext. 2001½ info@cityofmalden.org
Strong Past…Proud Future
o Increasing the density bonus for developers who comply with IZ ordinance 
from 1:1 to 2:1. This will hopefully make building affordable housing more 
attractive to developers.
o Lastly, a height bonus.
No big updates or movements on inclusionary zoning right now, but we will 
definitely have an update after November 10th city council meeting.
b. CPC Meeting and Public Hearing on Community Housing Projects
Mollie noted that this meeting is being held right after this meeting this evening. We will 
be sharing Malden’s affordable housing needs, current funding sources, anticipatory 
funding sources, and updates on each project that has Trust funds. Mollie noted that we 
will also be starting the application for Fiscal Year 2027 CPC application funds. Mollie 
will share how this went at next Trust Fund meeting on November 18th.
5. Affordable Housing Program Updates
a. Office of Housing Stability
Mollie noted that the Office of Housing Stability is doing very well. Noted that she met 
with Heather last week to get to know each other better. The Office of Housing Stability 
at Housing Families continues to be a resource for Malden residents. They offer 
advocacy, advice, and referrals. They run two weekly Lawyer for the Day programs in 
both courts that handle eviction cases for Malden. They also reach out to all Malden 
tenants with upcoming court dates to invite them to their weekly Eviction Defense clinic. 
They run a weekly Housing Task Force meeting with other local providers. They are 
continuing to partner with New England Law School on eviction sealing efforts. They are
planning an eviction records sealing clinic at the individual shelter on Broadway next 
month.
b. Development Projects
1. 245 Bryant Street (Asian Community Development Corporation)
Mollie recapped that during the Planning Board meeting on September 9th, the initial 
Board vote failed to secure the necessary supermajority, then there was a reconsideration 
motion that met the supermajority threshold, but that reconsideration vote was actually 
invalid under Section C.1.a of the Rules and Procedures of the Malden Planning Board so
the approval was revoked. ACDC is strategizing how to move forward and exploring 
other avenues
2. 213 Main Street (Asian Community Development Corporation)
Mollie noted that the weekly closing calls with them are going very well. They are 
closing on November 2nd, and have a groundbreaking ceremony scheduled for later that 
month, too. Mollie said we are excited to see this project cross the finish line soon. 
Mollie to make sure the team is invited to the groundbreaking ceremony.
3. Overlook Ridge (Winn Development)
Mollie delivered update that this project received $4 million from the MBTA 
Communities Catalyst Fund for the Overlook Ridge Drive Road improvement and $7 
million from the MBTA Communities Catalyst Fund for Overlook Ridge’s 14B project.
City of Malden, MA
215 Pleasant Street, Malden, MA 02148 ½ Phone: 781-397-7000 Ext. 2001½ info@cityofmalden.org
Strong Past…Proud Future
As a reminder, the 14B project pertains to the affordable homeownership project of 50 
units.
Mollie noted that this Trust is working on lot 13B, the affordable rental portion of the 
development. WinnDevelopment will be applying for funds to EOHLC sometime in 
2027. 
Mayor asked when there may be groundbreaking for this project. Mollie noted that she 
does not know when that will be at this time but will ask for an update from 
WinnDevelopment before the next meeting and provide that update to the team. Mayor 
asked Mollie to confirm the amount of homeownership units coming to the site and Mollie
confirmed it will be 50 units of homeownership. 
Dan asked two questions. He first sked when the project will be looking to receive the 
funds from the Trust fund. Mollie said she will update Trustees with this soon. Dan also 
asked for the 13B parcel ID. Mollie said she will send the parcel that is specific to the 
Trust funds to Dan.
4. 105 Salem Street (Volunteers of America)
Mollie noted that this project received $600,000 from the Underutilized Properties 
Program which is part of the statewide Community One Stop for Growth program. 
Reminded the team that this will be 12 affordable studio units for veterans by the 
Volunteers of America. Jane and Mollie met with them in-person on October 15th and had
a physical tour of the property. ISD inspected their building integrity, and it all looked 
good. They anticipate closing in Summer of 2027. Mollie noted that project is moving 
right along. Jane mentioned that Matt from VOA said that anybody from the Board can 
have a tour if they’d like. 
Mayor asked Mollie to confirm that it will be 12 affordable studio units. Jane noted that 
in their initial proposal, the project was going to be 10 affordable but now the 
development team will be providing all affordable units.
Angie asked a question regarding whether the vets will be living independently or if they 
will have more intense case management. Mollie confirmed supportive services will be 
on-site, but will be a mix of independent living, supportive services, community space for 
gathering. Jane added that it is unclear if supportive services will be staffed on a full-
time or part-time basis, but it will be largely independent living. 
6. Adjournment
Roxanne Reddington-Wilde made a motion to adjourn and was seconded by 
Catherine Price. Mayor initiated a final roll call of Trustees. All Trustees voted in 
favor and the meeting was adjourned at 5:23 PM.
